title: Millifluidics for Chemical Synthesis and Time-resolved Mechanistic Studies
protocol: Purchase a millifluidic chip made of polyester terephthalate polymer from Microplumbers Microsciences LLC.
Use FEP Tubing with dimensions of 0.25 mm I.D., 1/16 in O.D., for connecting the chip to the pump.
Test pumps with water as solvent at different pressures prior to the experiment to correlate with corresponding flow rates (ml/hr).
Rinse the millifluidic reactor and tubing with deionized water before initiation of the experiment.
Dissolve 174 mg of copper(II) nitrate in 28 ml of nanopure water.
Dissolve 610 mg of O-[2-(3-mercaptopropionylamino)ethyl]-O'-methylpolyethylene glycol in the solution from the previous step.
Prepare a solution containing 111 mg of sodium borohydride and 102 mg of sodium hydroxide in 28 ml of nanopure water, adjusting pH to ~13.
Connect one vial containing copper(II) nitrate and polyethylene glycol solution with one input channel of the millifluidic reactor.
Connect another vial containing sodium borohydride and sodium hydroxide solution with the other input channel of the millifluidic reactor.
Purge both solutions with nitrogen before connecting to the reactor.
Flow both solutions simultaneously within the millifluidic reactor at different flow-rates corresponding to pressures of 50 mbar, 100 mbar, 200 mbar, and 300 mbar.
Collect the resulting UCNCs in a glass vial at the outlet of the millifluidic reactor.
Purge the collected solution with nitrogen.
Store the solution under nitrogen.
Use high precision, fully automated, pulsation free syringe pumps to flow the liquids within the chip.
Test the pumps with water as solvent at different flow-rates prior to the experiment.
Prepare standard solutions of HAuCl4.3H2O (10 mmol, 118.2 mg/30 ml) and DMSA (20 mmol, 109.2 mg/30 ml) with sodium hydroxide in nanopure water to reach a pH of 12.
Feed the HAuCl4.3H2O solution through one syringe into the millifluidic chip at a constant flow-rate of 10 ml/hr using the automated pump.
Feed the DMSA solution through another syringe into the millifluidd chip at a constant flow-rate of 10 ml/hr using the automated pump.
Couple the millifluidic chip to the synchrotron beam line using a metal stage with XYZ directional movement.
Collect XAS data at different zones on the chip as solutions are pumped through.
Obtain chloroauric acid (HAuCl4.3H2O), meso-2,3-dimercaptosuccinic acid (DMSA), sodium borohydride, 4-nitrophenol, and 4-aminophenol for the experiment.
Prepare standard solutions of HAuCl4.3H2O (10 mmol, 118.2 mg/30 ml) in nanopure water for catalyst preparation.
Prepare standard solutions of DMSA (20 mmol, 109.2 mg/30 ml) in nanopure water for catalyst preparation.
Prepare standard solutions of NaBH4 (10 mmol, 11.34 mg/30 ml) in nanopure water for catalyst preparation.
Take 10 ml of HAuCl4 into a vial.
Flow the HAuCl4 within the chip using the hand-held millifluidic device at a flow-rate of 12 ml/hr for 45 min.
Take 10 ml of DMSA solution into another vial.
Flow the DMSA within the chip using the hand-held millifluidic device at a flow-rate of 12 ml/hr for 45 min.
Flow 10 mmol NaBH4 within the chip at a flow-rate of 12 ml/hr for 15 min to reduce Au(I) to Au(0).
Wash the chip with nanopure water for 30 min at a flow-rate of 12 ml/hr before conducting catalysis experiments.
Mix 15 ml of 9 x 10^-5 mol solution of 4-NP with 3.3 ml of 0.65 mol NaBH4 solution to form 4-nitrophenolate ion (4-NPI).
Pass the resultant solution over the gold catalyst within the chip at a constant flow rate of 5 ml/hr.
Analyze the UV-Vis spectra of the collected products in the wavelength range of 250-500 nm.
Obtain the calibration curve of 4-NPI by plotting the experimentally observed absorption intensity (I) of 4-NPI at different standard concentrations.
Estimate the catalytic activity by finding the difference in initial and final concentrations of the reactant from the calibration curve.
